slides.title: Introduction to Python
bullets: High-level, general-purpose programming language.
Known for highly readable, English-like syntax.
Interpreted language (code is executed line-by-line, not compiled).
Dynamically typed (you do not need to declare variable types).
Widely used in Web Development, Data Science, AI, and Automation.

slides.title: Setup and Execution
bullets: Installation: Download the interpreter from python.org.
Code Editor: Use IDEs like VS Code or PyCharm.
Execution: Run Python files (.py) using the interpreter.
The `print()` function is used to display output (e.g., `print('Hello')`).
Comments are denoted by the `#` symbol for single-line notes.

slides.title: Variables and Data Types
bullets: Variables are named containers used to store data values.
Naming Conventions: Must start with a letter or underscore, cannot use keywords.
Key Immutable Data Types:
Integers (`int`): Whole numbers (e.g., 5, -10).
Floats (`float`): Decimal numbers (e.g., 3.14).
Strings (`str`): Text, enclosed in single or double quotes.
Booleans (`bool`): True or False.

slides.title: Operators
bullets: Operators perform operations on variables and values.
Assignment Operator: `=` (used to assign a value to a variable).
Arithmetic Operators: `+` (add), `-` (subtract), `*` (multiply), `/` (divide), `%` (modulo/remainder).
Comparison Operators: Used to compare values, resulting in a Boolean (True/False):
`==` (Equal to)
`>` (Greater than), `<` (Less than)
`!=` (Not equal to)

slides.title: Control Flow: Conditionals
bullets: Allows the program to make decisions based on conditions.
`if` statement: Executes code only if the condition is True.
`elif` (Else If): Checks additional conditions if the preceding ones were False.
`else`: Executes if none of the preceding conditions were True.
Indentation (4 spaces) is mandatory to define code blocks.

slides.title: Control Flow: Loops
bullets: Loops allow execution of a block of code multiple times.
`for` loop: Used for iterating over a sequence (list, tuple, dictionary, string, or range).
`while` loop: Executes a block of code as long as a condition remains True.
The `break` statement can stop the loop entirely.
The `continue` statement skips the current iteration and moves to the next.

slides.title: Introduction to Data Structures
bullets: Lists: Ordered, mutable (changeable) collections; defined by square brackets `[]`.
Lists support indexing (starting at 0) and methods like `.append()` and `.pop()`.
Tuples: Ordered, immutable (unchangeable) collections; defined by parentheses `()`.
Dictionaries: Unordered collections of key-value pairs; defined by curly braces `{}`.

slides.title: Functions
bullets: Functions are blocks of reusable code designed to perform a specific task.
Defined using the `def` keyword followed by the function name.
Can accept inputs (parameters) inside the parentheses.
The `return` statement is used to send a value back to the caller.
Functions must be defined before they are called/executed.
